questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had always wanted to study in the U.S at some point throughout my education, so I thought taking a semester on exchange in the U.S as part of my masters would be a great opportunity to do so. Moreover, I had never been to California before, and I have quite a few contacts there too. UC Davis also has a high academic level, which I also took into account.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: When I arrived, I had already received alot of information from the University of Copenhagen and UC Davis, which made my arrival easy. However, there were certain e-mails and info that I couldn't find on my own, but that both faculties were open to help with either way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an orientation day where we met faculty staff and the dean of the law school. Our first week of class was with the 1L J.D students  (1-years), so we were on fairly equal level and got a nice introduction to the legal landscape of the U.S.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a VERY difficult time finding a place to stay. In my experience, it is a problem arriving as an exchange student, because the majority of housing options is based on signing a one year lease. This puts a lot of risk on exchange students (if you decide to sign such a lease), as you will be responsible for finding someone to take over your lease. There are rooms available, but many of them are "overpriced" compared to expectations. It is not being picky, but simply having a realistic budget for the trip, where a room in a house that costs $1.800 a month is too much. Moreover, I found it to be a disadvantage to be a male searching for housing. 80% of the Facebook posts and posts on similar websites said "female only" if you wanted to stay there. My recommendation would be to search for housing early. I though I was early, but many people had already made arrangments before me. Therefore, it is a good idea to make posts and inquiries before someone else does.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: At UC Davis, it does not make a huge difference in terms of transportation to campus, as it is a very bike friendly town. (I think it is the "bike capital" of California). I lived as far away from campus as possible (within Davis), but it only took me 20 minutes to get to class. One thing that off-campus housing lacks is the social aspect of living close to other students. Streets, cafes and supermarkets are all more lively when they are closer to campus. Plus, it is more common to meet people you know from class. However, you can find housing complexes that are meant for students, even though they are off-campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience was a 1/5, but the availability to students in general is pretty good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration itself was quite straight forward. However, the courses that I first applied to after thorough research were all full, even though I did it within the deadline. I ended up having a meeting with a faculty member in order to find new courses. I ended up being able to shape my preferred schedule, but the courses themselves were not ones that I would have dreamt of having in the first place. However, I ended up enjoying the courses I took. The faculty staff also lets you know about waitlists, how to get on them and the likelyhood of getting the course. You also have the opportunity to take more classes than you need, and then drop them if you dont like them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, the faculty staff was helpful in terms of any problems associated with course registration. E.g. they were helpful in terms of making sure that the amount of credits needed to fulfill the exchange ECTS requirements were met.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not successful in registering for any of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont have any really, as I couldn't help that the courses were full, and I did it before the deadline. However, I would recommend having alternatives in case you don't get your 1st or even 2nd priorities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Well, the level of education in the U.S isn't divided into BA and MA, but undergraduate and graduate. Since Law is exclusively a graduate course, I would say mainly MA courses are taken at UC Davis. However, there is a difference between "bar courses" (used for the bar exam) and non bar courses. Of the four courses that I had, only one was a bar course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. The socratic method (cold calling) is very common at the UC universities and in Law school in the U.S in general. At UCPH this is against the rules, so it took some getting used to. Also, many professors have zero laptop policies and some dont even use powerpoint slides. Moreover, at UCPH one's grade is based entirely on the outcome of an exam. At UC Davis it is a combination of class participation, assignments and the final exam. Moreover, there isn't an actual "exam period" as we are used to. Classes end only about a week before finals start. This was a source of stress for some, but the professors do take it into account when correcting finals.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Environmental Law, Constitutional Law II (equal protection and first amendment), Alternative Dispute Resolution & Election Law: Voting Rights Seminar.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found Environmental Law quite relevant, even though I was sceptical at first. It is a very specific subject, so probably not a good way to get a basic understanding of the legal system in the U.S. I really liked Alternative Dispute Resolution, and would highly recommend this. Constitutional Law II was good to get a broader understanding of the U.S legal system, and the professor is a well renowned scholar within the topic in the US. However, he did not use powerpoints and had no laptop policy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The faculty at UC Davis had some strange one time fee payments that we had to pay, where a few cost over 1,000DKK. Books were more expensive than they had said the estimate prices are. I was also scammed for two months rent, and had to pay this double.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books (more expensive), Cellular data (less expensive), Food and groceries (more expensive).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I played football (soccer) during my time at UC Davis, which was great! Both for King Hall FC and in the intramural tournament.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The ARC (Schools Recreational centre) had climbing, basketball, badminton, squash, gym, table tennis, crossfit, volleyball and boxing available. This was free through the school.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Playing football for King Hall FC, as it is so much fun and a great way to meet new people, also across years of Law.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: San Francisco, Napa Valley, Lake Tahoe, LA, Yosemite, Las Vegas, Santa Barbara, Santa Cruz, Hearst Castle, Solvang, Sacramento, G-Street Wunderbar and Parkside. College football is also cool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it pretty easy, and enjoyed being a real californian for 4 months!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, either sport or academic, go out in the weekends and travel when you can. In general take every experience you are offered!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Cold calling, no laptop policy, legal english vocabulary, the fact that sales tax and tipping is calculated after the price and that people at law school (in some instances) would not really speak to exchange students, because we are there for a short period only. (But you can help that by being social).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that people are open and welcoming, the weather (until late October), all the beautiful sights to see in California, the cars, the restaurants, the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Know that Davis is quite a small university town, so there is only a limited amount of things to do. There are nice bars, cafes, stores, restaurants and sports faciliteis, but sometimes it is needed to take a trip to San Francisco or another location that has more going on. This does, however, make it a great town to concentrate for studying in.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I covered it :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and getting the chance to live in a foreign country for a longer period of time. Being in California for 4 months, though not being too long, you are there long enough to gain alot of knowledge about the state, the people, the cities and the life in general. Also, being able to attend courses that are in English with people who have had English courses all their lives, and still being able to follow their level.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
